rounds.analysis: Hypothesis: L21h6 is a successor head. Its OV circuit maps the token it attends to onto that token's successor. Evidence: it has the largest ablation effect on sequence prompts, and the oracle swap gives two-steps-ahead answers 92% of the time. On lookup prompts it barely attends to the queried value (0.01). If it is redirected from the final position to the queried value, it should write successor(value) into the residual. L22h7 is a late copy head that writes the value itself, so damping it may be needed. Removing L21h6 costs only +0.043 WikiText, well under budget. An alternative test: transplant h6's OV into L21h8, which already attends to the queried value (0.24). These candidates separate the QK-redirect route from the OV-transplant route, and test whether suppressing the competing copy head matters.

candidates.rationale: Core test: reprogram L21h6 QK to attend from final to queried_value. Use slow RoPE dims and an other_values contrast so it picks the right line's value. Amplify the output modestly.

Same redirect with a stronger gain. Also remove the downstream copy head L22h7 so the literal value competes less with its successor. Layers 16 and 19 are kept intact so h6's input statistics still encode the lookup.

OV-transplant route: L21h8 already attends to the queried value. Give its value group and output columns h6's successor OV, which keeps h6 itself intact. This tests whether the successor mapping lives in OV alone.

rounds.analysis: Redirecting L21h6 from final to queried_value works: successor rate went from 0.035 to 0.48. Transplanting its OV into h8 gave only 0.125, so the successor effect needs h6's own attention and possibly its value group. Two limits remain. Attention on the value is only 0.29, and the literal value still wins about 30% of the time. Removing L22h7 added nothing to successor rate (0.49) and cost WikiText. Hypotheses: (a) sharper, more selective attention would lift the rate, via lower ridge and higher rank, or via the other_positions contrast; (b) layer-21 copy heads h8 and h15, which attend to the value and write it literally, compete with the successor output. WikiText is 3.33 against a 3.64 limit, so there is budget left.

candidates.rationale: Sharpen attention: ridge 0.1, rank 64 in low band, other_values contrast, gain 2. L22h7 kept intact to isolate the attention effect.
Competition test: same redirect as R1, gain 2, but remove the same-layer copy heads L21h8 and L21h15 (both attend to the value; ablation cost is tiny) and L22h7.
Contrast test: other_positions contrast with ridge 0.1, rank 64. Checks whether contrasting against all positions, not only other values, gives more attention mass on the queried value. Gain 2.

rounds.analysis: The successor rate plateaus near 0.48 whatever the attention sharpness or gain. In R2P2, attention of 0.61 gave 0.45, so attention mass is not the bottleneck. The losers are the literal value (about 25–30%) and other answers (about 22%). Low ridge raises WikiText and hurts sequence continuation, so ridge stays at 1.0. This round tests three mechanisms. (1) Upstream literal-copy suppression: the literal value may already be in the final residual from L16h14 and L19h5 before layer 21, so ablate them. (2) Reading the queried_arrow position instead: its residual already encodes the predicted value, which may be closer to what h6's OV expects in native sequence use. (3) A clean OV-sufficiency test that leaves h6 intact for text and sequences: program fresh attention into L21h0, give it h6's OV, and silence h1, which shares group 0 and would otherwise output garbage. R1P2 confounded OV with h8's diffuse native attention.

candidates.rationale: Literal-suppression test. Use R1P0, the best and cheapest redirect, plus ablation of the earliest strong value-copy heads L16h14 and L19h5. If the literal value is injected upstream, the successor rate should rise. If h6's query relies on that copied info, the attention on the value will drop, which is also informative.

Source-position test: attend to the queried arrow, whose residual predicts the value, instead of the value token itself. Uses the other_positions contrast at ridge 1.0 for sharper but cheaper attention.

OV-sufficiency test that preserves native h6. Program L21h0 (group 0) to attend from final to the queried value, give it h6's value rows and output columns, and remove h1, which shares the altered group. Sequence continuation and WikiText should stay near the unedited values if this works.

rounds.analysis: R3P2 is the key result. A fresh head (L21h0) with programmed attention plus h6's OV gives 0.445 successor. Sequence continuation stays at 1.0 and WikiText at 3.229, the cheapest so far. So the successor map lives in h6's OV and only needs targeted attention; R1P2 failed because h8's native attention was untargeted. Attention mass (0.62) and gain do not seem to be the bottleneck; the literal value still wins about 25%. Hypothesis: the total successor signal is limited per head, so adding parallel successor heads with h6's OV should push successor logits above the literal. Tests: (A) two clean successor heads (h0 and h14 with h6's OV), silencing h1 and h15, where h15 is also a literal copy head; (B) the clean h0 head plus redirected native h6; (C) the clean h0 head with the other_values contrast and higher gain, to check gain saturation in the cheap setting.

candidates.rationale: Additivity with native h6 preserved: two fresh successor heads in groups 0 and 7. Silencing h15 also removes a literal-copy head. If the rate rises well above 0.45 with WikiText near 3.25, this is the frozen candidate.

Additivity using native h6 too: the clean h0 successor head plus the R1P0 redirect of h6 itself. This tests whether two successor heads with different attention solutions add up, at the cost of h6's native sequence role.
Single clean head, varying the contrast (other_values, the best for h6 in R1) and gain 2.5. This checks whether output magnitude limits the clean route once native h6 is untouched.

rounds.analysis: Successor heads add up. Clean h0 (h6's OV) plus redirected native h6 gave 0.615, the best so far. A single clean head improved from 0.445 at gain 1.5 to 0.55 at gain 2.5, though the contrast also changed between those runs. WikiText is 3.413 against a 3.644 limit, so there is room to raise output gains. This final round pushes the two-head combination, which fits in 6 ops. P0 raises clean h0 to gain 2.5 with other_positions attention (0.62 mass) and keeps h6 at 1.5. P1 uses other_values attention for both heads, with h0 at 2.5 and h6 at 2.0. P2 is P0 plus removal of the cheap literal-copy head L21h15, which costs only +0.007 WikiText. That tests whether suppressing the literal answer helps once successor signal is strong. All three stay in layer 21 and use the general h6 OV, so they should transfer to other value types.

candidates.rationale: R4P1 with the clean successor head amplified to gain 2.5, using sharp other_positions attention; native h6 redirect kept at 1.5.
Both heads use other_values attention, which gave 0.55 alone at gain 2.5. Native h6 is raised to gain 2.0. Tests whether the other_values attention solution adds better than the other_positions one.
P0 plus removal of the literal-copy head L21h15 (+0.007 WikiText). Tests whether suppressing the competing literal answer helps once the successor signal is large.
